metadata.title: Claude, Buyer List.
metadata.purpose: nbb (Teardown) cut of claude-liam-buyer-list — take the buyer-list skill apart, show the machinery (one folder, one SKILL.md, linear steps), and judge the design choice (readable page over hidden logic) that ships with it.
metadata.carry_out: A Skill doesn't make Claude smarter — it makes Claude follow your steps, in order, every time.

beats.narration_text: Liam, in for Bear. You'd think buyer-list is an app with some algorithm inside it that goes out and finds buyers. It isn't. It's a folder with a text file, and Claude reads that file first — before it does anything else. So the real question isn't what the app does. It's what the file tells Claude to do.

props.text:
How does the
buyer-list app
find buyers?

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. The skill is one folder — buyer-list — with one file inside it: SKILL.md. That file is the whole instruction set, written in plain English. No hidden code, no compiled logic, nothing trained on your workflow. Claude reads the markdown, then does what the markdown says. The design choice is severe: they made the program readable to you, not just to Claude — because if you can't read it, you can't fix it.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in a Steps section — literally a numbered list. Claude reads step one, does it, reads step two, does it. Linear execution. They optimized for you being able to predict what will happen next, at the expense of anything clever.

What buyer-list actually does: build a universe of potential acquirers for a sell-side M&A deal, sort strategic buyers from financial buyers, and rank the outreach order. That's the whole scope. Because Claude follows the page exactly, you get the same result every run — that's the trade-off they took. What you don't get: anything the page doesn't say. It ranks by the criteria written down; it cannot judge criteria that aren't written down.

props.heading: What the page says, exactly.
props.body: Build a buyer universe for sell-side M&A.
props.sparkLine: Same page, same result, every run.

beats.narration_text: A Skill doesn't make Claude smarter — it makes Claude follow your steps, in order, every time.

props.quote: A Skill doesn't make Claude smarter — it makes Claude follow your steps, in order, every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into any frontier LLM — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini: 'Explain, in plain English, what a Claude Skill is — then, if I gave you a three-step SKILL.md for making coffee, walk me through exactly how you'd read and follow it, step by step, before you start.' Watch what it does with that last part. If it reads the three steps out loud before doing anything, that's the mechanism working — the file is the program, and it's reading the program back to you. Go deeper: ask it to write you a SKILL.md for one boring recurring task you already do, and try handing that file to a colleague — the file's usefulness is whether they get the same result you do.
